0x221cc6c3ee6df4050892e858efcc78a8709224.title: Konkani ↔ English Translator
0x221cc6c3ee6df4050892e858efcc78a8709224.summary: An open-weights translation model for Konkani, a low-resource Indian language with no production-grade MT. Trained from community-contributed parallel text.
0x221cc6c3ee6df4050892e858efcc78a8709224.about: Konkani is spoken by ~2.5M people across coastal India but is effectively invisible to commercial translation systems — there is no clean, openly licensed parallel corpus large enough to fine-tune on. This Forge pools sentence pairs, glossaries, and proofreading effort from native speakers and Konkani-language institutions, scores each contribution by its measured effect on held-out translation quality, and mints proportional ownership of the resulting model. The output is a permanently free Ingot that anyone can run.
datasetGuidance: Sentence-aligned Konkani↔English pairs (news, literature, conversation)
Devanagari and Romi script both welcome — tag the script
Native-speaker proofreading passes on machine-drafted pairs
Domain glossaries (legal, medical, civic) with attested sources
No copyrighted text without a clear redistribution license
audience: Native Konkani speakers and translators contributing parallel text
Language institutions donating digitised corpora
GPU providers running the fine-tune jobs
Backers funding eval-set curation and proofreading bounties

useCases.title: Civic & government access
useCases.body: Translate public-health and government notices into Konkani at near-zero marginal cost.

useCases.title: Education tooling
useCases.body: Power reading apps and bilingual learning material for Konkani-medium schools.

useCases.title: Composable lineage
useCases.body: Downstream Forges can fork this Ingot for Konkani ASR or summarisation and inherit attribution.

0x2414b96056adef9aee1523b846f1a94656399a.title: MSA Risk-Clause Classifier
0x2414b96056adef9aee1523b846f1a94656399a.summary: A contract-intelligence model that flags risky clauses in software Master Service Agreements — uncapped liability, auto-renewal, IP assignment, unilateral termination.
0x2414b96056adef9aee1523b846f1a94656399a.about: Reviewing a software MSA is slow, expensive, and inconsistent across reviewers. This Forge trains a classifier that reads a clause and labels it by risk category and severity, so legal and procurement teams can triage a 40-page agreement in minutes. Contributors supply labelled clauses from real (redacted) agreements and adjudicate disagreements; ownership of the model mints in proportion to how much each contribution moved held-out F1.
datasetGuidance: Redacted clauses labelled by risk category + severity (1–5)
Cover liability, indemnity, IP, termination, renewal, data terms
Include benign clauses as negatives — not just risky ones
Two-reviewer adjudication on contested labels
Strip all party names and commercial figures before upload
audience: Contract lawyers and legal-ops teams contributing labelled clauses
Procurement reviewers adjudicating edge cases
Compute providers for the fine-tune sweep
Backers underwriting the gold-standard eval set

useCases.title: First-pass contract triage
useCases.body: Surface the 5 clauses a human must read first, instead of all 60.

useCases.title: Procurement guardrails
useCases.body: Block auto-renewal and uncapped-liability terms from slipping through unreviewed.

useCases.title: Inference via the proxy
useCases.body: Call the trained Ingot through Foundry's OpenAI-compatible endpoint from any review tool.

0x5d08d97de140e79cdac032e10e36fe3b86930a.title: Chemistry-Paper Retrieval Embeddings
0x5d08d97de140e79cdac032e10e36fe3b86930a.summary: A dense embedding model tuned for semantic retrieval over chemistry and materials-science literature, where general-purpose embeddings miss reaction and compound nuance.
0x5d08d97de140e79cdac032e10e36fe3b86930a.about: Researchers searching chemistry corpora are failed by generic embeddings: they collapse distinct reaction mechanisms and confuse compounds with similar names. This Forge fine-tunes an embedding model on contributed query→relevant-passage pairs mined from real literature search sessions, so retrieval ranks the paper a chemist actually wanted. Ownership mints proportionally to each contribution's measured lift in retrieval accuracy.
datasetGuidance: Query → relevant-passage pairs from real literature search
Hard negatives: near-miss passages that look relevant but aren't
Span organic, inorganic, and materials sub-domains
Abstract-level granularity is fine; full-text spans are better
Only openly licensed or self-authored passages
audience: Chemists and librarians contributing labelled retrieval pairs
Research groups donating anonymised search logs
Compute providers for contrastive fine-tuning
Backers funding annotation of hard negatives

useCases.title: Better literature search
useCases.body: Drop-in embedding upgrade for RAG over chemistry corpora.

useCases.title: Patent & prior-art discovery

0xc39be4476c4cac6911d0894a549497a947462d.title: Clinical Note De-Identification
0xc39be4476c4cac6911d0894a549497a947462d.summary: A model that detects and redacts protected health information in free-text clinical notes, so hospitals can share data for research without leaking patient identity.
0xc39be4476c4cac6911d0894a549497a947462d.about: De-identification is the gate on every clinical-data-sharing project, and off-the-shelf PII scrubbers miss the long tail of clinical phrasing. This Forge trains a sequence labeller on contributed, expert-redacted notes — names, dates, MRNs, locations, rare identifiers — and scores contributions by their effect on held-out recall, because in de-id a single miss is a breach. The resulting Ingot is openly runnable so smaller institutions aren't priced out.
datasetGuidance: Synthetic or fully consented notes only — never real PHI
Token-level spans for every identifier type
Cover rare identifiers: device IDs, rare locations, kin names
Include hard negatives (clinical terms that look like names)
Two-annotator agreement before a span is accepted
audience: Clinical NLP annotators contributing labelled spans
Hospitals donating consented or synthetic note sets
Compute providers for the labelling-model fine-tune
Backers funding the adversarial recall eval

useCases.title: Unblock data sharing
useCases.body: Redact note corpora to a defensible standard before research release.

useCases.title: Pipeline pre-processing
useCases.body: Run as the first stage of any downstream clinical-NLP Forge.

useCases.title: Audit trail
useCases.body: Every redaction decision is reproducible from the on-chain attestation.

0xeff6fc79b6d3f361602e745dc7d1c7a9492b50.title: Solidity Vulnerability Explainer
0xeff6fc79b6d3f361602e745dc7d1c7a9492b50.summary: A code model that reads a Solidity function and explains likely vulnerability classes in plain English — reentrancy, unchecked math, access-control gaps.
0xeff6fc79b6d3f361602e745dc7d1c7a9492b50.about: Most smart-contract bugs are re-discoveries of known patterns, but junior auditors and protocol devs lack the pattern library in their head. This Forge trains a generation model on contributed (vulnerable snippet → explanation + fixed version) triples drawn from public audit reports and CTF challenges. Contributions are scored on how much they improve held-out explanation quality, and the Ingot becomes a free second pair of eyes for every Solidity author.
datasetGuidance: Triples: vulnerable snippet → explanation → fixed version
Cite the vulnerability class (SWC / DASP where applicable)
Cover reentrancy, access control, arithmetic, oracle, DoS
Include safe look-alikes so the model doesn't over-flag
Public audit reports / CTFs only — no client-confidential code
audience: Auditors contributing annotated findings
Protocol engineers donating fixed-bug pairs
GPU providers running the QLoRA fine-tune
Backers funding the held-out explanation rubric

useCases.title: Inline review assistant
useCases.body: Explain risk in a diff before it reaches a human auditor.

0xcaf8469cdbb71bc9db60f60236f188267ea925.title: Spoken-Hindi Intent Classifier
0xcaf8469cdbb71bc9db60f60236f188267ea925.summary: An intent classifier for code-mixed spoken Hindi-English (Hinglish), built for voice interfaces that India's existing NLU stacks handle poorly.
0xcaf8469cdbb71bc9db60f60236f188267ea925.about: Voice products in India have to understand Hinglish — Hindi and English mixed within a single utterance, transliterated a dozen different ways. General intent models trained on clean English collapse on this. This Forge pools transcribed utterances labelled with intent and slots, weighted toward real spoken data, and scores contributions by held-out accuracy on a code-mixed test set. The Ingot ships free so small Indian-language voice teams aren't gated on a vendor.
datasetGuidance: Transcribed Hinglish utterances with intent + slot labels
Keep natural code-switching — do not normalise to one language
Cover multiple transliteration spellings of the same word
Real spoken data preferred over written/synthetic
Speaker consent required for any human-recorded data
audience: Annotators labelling intents and slots on Hinglish speech
Voice teams donating consented, transcribed utterances
Compute providers for the LoRA fine-tune
Backers funding the code-mixed evaluation set

useCases.title: Voice assistants
useCases.body: Route Hinglish commands correctly in consumer voice products.

useCases.title: IVR & support bots
useCases.body: Understand mixed-language customer intents without a vendor NLU.
